 Mr. Rakesh Singh Rajput - P.L. for State.

Order 
This is sixth bail application filed on behalf of the applicants under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

2. The applicant is in custody since 12.4.2021 in connection with Crime No.115/2024 registered at P.S.-Gunaur, District Panna (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 304B, 498A of IPC and sections 3 /4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that marriage of applicant was solemnized with deceased on 5.5.2023 as per social Customs.
After marriage, deceased went to her in-law's house from where she returned to her maternal home after staying at her maternal home for 15 days.
Applicant along with co-accused persons harassed and on account of aforesaid harassment, deceased committed suicide.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant is in jail since 12.4.2021.
It is also urged that offence under Section 304B of IPC is not made out and it does not come within the purview of the said offence.
It is also urged that omnibus and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42741 2 MCRC-29770-2025 general allegations have been leveled against the applicant.
There are no injuries have been on the person of deceased.
Harassment and demand of dowry has not been proved in the instant case.

Learned counsel for the applicant has relied upon Uma Shankar @ Chotu Ravendra @ Sonu Chaudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169489473/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is delay in trial and material witnesses have been examined.
The trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicants be released on bail pending the trial.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail.
6. Perusal of the record of the case reveals that earlier application of the applicant was dismissed on 12.03.2025 by a detailed order on merits.
There is no substantial change of circumstance after dismissal of earlier bail application on merits.
As per submissions of learned counsel for the applicant himself, out of 17 witnesses, 11 witnesses have been examined.
Applicant is the husband of the deceased.
In the instant case, marriage of applicant was solemnized with deceased on 5.5.2023 and deceased committed suicide on 16.3.2024.
7. Hence, in view of aforesaid, no case for bail is made out.
8. Accordingly, this application is dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi Ravendra @ Sonu Chaudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169489473/
